entries.definition: The independent regulator of health and adult social care in England.
entries.source: Health and Social Care Act 2008 (established the Care Quality Commission)

entries.full_term: Department of Health and Social Care
entries.definition: The UK government department responsible for health and adult social care policy in England.
entries.source: GOV.UK — Department of Health and Social Care.

entries.full_term: Department for Levelling Up, Housing and Communities
entries.definition: UK government department from 2021-2024, succeeded by the Ministry of Housing, Communities and Local Government (MHCLG). Co-funder with The National Lottery Community Fund of the Changing Futures Programme.
entries.source: GOV.UK — Department for Levelling Up, Housing and Communities (renamed the Ministry of Housing, Communities and Local Government in 2024).

entries.definition: The senior officer each local authority must appoint (jointly with the Secretary of State) to lead its public health functions.
The UK government department responsible for welfare, pensions and employment support.
entries.source: GOV.UK — Department for Work and Pensions.

entries.definition: The statutory NHS body that plans and commissions health services for a defined area.
The statutory joint committee of an integrated care system that agrees a health-and-care strategy for the area, bringing the NHS and local partners together.
entries.source: Health and Care Act 2022 (integrated care partnerships)

entries.definition: A specialist domestic-abuse support worker for survivors at high risk of harm.
An employment model in which specialists are embedded in mental-health teams; the strongest-evidenced employment intervention for adults with severe mental illness.
entries.source: Evidence-based supported employment (Centre for Mental Health).

entries.definition: The statutory assessment of the current and future health and care needs of a local population, prepared for each area by the responsible local authority and its partner integrated care board — discharged locally through the Health and Wellbeing Board.
entries.source: Local Government and Public Involvement in Health Act 2007, s.116

entries.definition: The multi-agency forum for managing the highest-risk domestic abuse cases.
entries.source: SafeLives — What is a MARAC? (SafeLives stewards the national MARAC model and holds the definition)

entries.definition: The unitary local authority for the Middlesbrough area.
The publicly funded health system, created by the National Health Service Act 1946 (operational 5 July 1948) and now governed by the consolidating National Health Service Act 2006.
entries.source: National Health Service Act 1946 (established the NHS; now consolidated in the NHS Act 2006)

entries.full_term: National Institute for Health and Care Research
entries.definition: The national funder of the Health Determinants Research Collaboration (HDRC) infrastructure.

entries.full_term: Redcar and Cleveland Voluntary Development Agency
entries.definition: The local infrastructure charity supporting voluntary and community groups across Redcar & Cleveland.
The unitary local authority for the Redcar and Cleveland area.

A Ministry of Housing, Communities and Local Government capital programme funding move-on accommodation for people who sleep rough or are at risk of doing so; a predecessor to later rough-sleeping programmes.
The unitary local authority for the Stockton-on-Tees area, in the Tees Valley.

entries.full_term: Tees, Esk and Wear Valleys NHS Foundation Trust
entries.definition: The specialist mental-health and learning-disability trust serving the Tees Valley.
entries.source: National Health Service Act 2006, s.30 (NHS foundation trusts; originally the Health and Social Care (Community Health and Standards) Act 2003)

entries.definition: The multi-agency statutory board that coordinates adult safeguarding across the Tees area.
The sub-regional combined authority covering the five Tees Valley boroughs (Middlesbrough, Redcar & Cleveland, Stockton-on-Tees, Hartlepool and Darlington), led by the Tees Valley Mayor.
entries.source: Tees Valley Combined Authority Order 2016 (SI 2016/449), under the Local Democracy, Economic Development and Construction Act 2009

entries.full_term: Voluntary, Community, Faith and Social Enterprise
aliases: voluntary, community, faith and social enterprise
entries.definition: Voluntary, Community, Faith and Social Enterprise — the collective term for charities, community groups, faith organisations and social enterprises.
The unitary local authority for the Borough of Darlington in the Tees Valley.
The unitary local authority for the Borough of Hartlepool in the Tees Valley.
The sustainable-transport charity and custodian of the National Cycle Network; 'Sustrans' is short for 'sustainable transport'.
The rural community council for the Tees Valley, supporting rural communities and voluntary organisations.
The regional infrastructure body representing and supporting the voluntary, community and social enterprise sector across the North East.

entries.full_term: National Association for Voluntary and Community Action
aliases: National Association for Voluntary and Community Action
entries.definition: The national membership body for local infrastructure organisations supporting the voluntary and community sector in England.
The NHS foundation trust providing 999 emergency and patient-transport ambulance services across the North East.
entries.source: North East Ambulance Service NHS Foundation Trust

entries.definition: The national body that led the NHS in England and oversaw commissioning; its functions are being brought back into the Department of Health and Social Care following the March 2025 decision to abolish it.
The NHS bodies that commissioned most local health services from 2013; abolished in July 2022 and replaced by Integrated Care Boards (ICBs).
The principal public agency for conducting criminal prosecutions in England and Wales, established under the Prosecution of Offences Act 1985.
The national governing body for tennis in Great Britain.
The UK government department responsible for education and children's services in England.
Collective term for children and young people, commonly used in health, education and social-care services.
A framework of environmental, social and governance criteria used to assess an organisation's wider impact and responsible practice.
A body that supports, develops and represents the local voluntary and community sector (for example a council for voluntary service); RCVDA is the LIO for Redcar & Cleveland.
Charities, community groups and other not-for-profit organisations; the narrower predecessor term to VCSE (which also includes social enterprise).
The transfer of land or buildings from public ownership (usually a local authority) to a community or voluntary organisation, at less than market value, to secure community benefit.

entries.full_term: Specific, Meaningful, Achievable, Relevant, Time-bound, Evaluate, Re-adjust
aliases: Specific, Meaningful, Achievable, Relevant, Time-bound, Evaluate, Re-adjust
entries.definition: A goal-setting mnemonic extending the SMART objectives framework with 'Evaluate' and 'Re-adjust' stages.

entries.full_term: Timely, Helpful, Respectful, Innovative, Values-based and Efficient
aliases: Timely, Helpful, Respectful, Innovative, Values-based and Efficient
entries.definition: A values mnemonic describing how services aim to work. Distinct from the local Thrive Partnership.
A non-profit provider of social housing (typically a housing association) registered with, and regulated by, the social housing regulator.

Local arrangements to provide emergency accommodation for people sleeping rough during severe weather; a discretionary, non-statutory response prompted by cold-weather and other severe-weather thresholds.
entries.source: MHCLG rough sleeping / cold weather provision guidance.

entries.definition: A coordinated, person-centred approach bringing the relevant workers around one individual to plan and deliver joined-up support.
The coordinated management of a town centre's environment, economy and activity, usually as a partnership between the local authority, businesses and other stakeholders.
An umbrella term for a range of abuses disproportionately affecting women and girls, including domestic abuse, sexual violence, stalking and so-called honour-based abuse.
entries.source: Home Office — Tackling Violence Against Women and Girls Strategy (2021).

entries.definition: A geographical management area of Jobcentre Plus, the part of the Department for Work and Pensions that delivers working-age benefits and employment support.
entries.source: Department for Work and Pensions — Jobcentre Plus.

entries.term: Limited Capability for Work and Work-Related Activity
entries.full_term: Limited Capability for Work and Work-Related Activity
aliases: Limited Capability for Work and Work-Related Activity
entries.definition: A Universal Credit determination that a claimant's health condition or disability so limits them that they are not expected to work or prepare for work, attracting an additional UC element.
entries.source: Welfare Reform Act 2012; Universal Credit Regulations 2013

entries.definition: A non-means-tested benefit that helps with the extra costs of a long-term health condition or disability; it replaced Disability Living Allowance for working-age adults.
A quality standard for supported-employment services helping disabled people and those with health conditions into work.
The single means-tested working-age benefit that replaces six legacy benefits including Housing Benefit, Income Support and tax credits.
A registered mental-health nurse who supports people with mental-health needs in the community; now more often titled community mental-health nurse.

entries.full_term: Children and Young People’s Improving Access to Psychological Therapies programme
aliases: Children and Young People’s Improving Access to Psychological Therapies programme
entries.definition: An NHS England programme to transform children and young people's mental-health services by embedding evidence-based psychological therapies and outcome monitoring.

entries.term: Child and Adolescent Mental Health Services
entries.full_term: Child and Adolescent Mental Health Services
aliases: Child and Adolescent Mental Health Services
entries.definition: NHS services that assess and treat children and young people with emotional, behavioural or mental-health difficulties.
An administrative code recording that a patient missed a booked appointment without notice; increasingly reframed as 'was not brought' for children.
An approach to public policy that systematically accounts for the health implications of decisions across all sectors, to improve health and reduce inequalities.
entries.source: World Health Organization — Health in All Policies.

entries.definition: A statutory local-authority committee bringing together the NHS, public health, adult social care and children's services to improve health and wellbeing and reduce inequalities.
entries.source: Health and Social Care Act 2012, s.194

entries.definition: A local executive group supporting the delivery of a Health and Wellbeing Board's priorities.
The framework used to assess, plan and coordinate care for people with more complex mental-health needs; now largely superseded by the Community Mental Health Framework.
entries.source: Department of Health — Care Programme Approach.

entries.definition: A statutory partnership of local 'responsible authorities' (police, local authority, fire, health and probation) that works to reduce crime, disorder and antisocial behaviour.
The statutory duty on relevant partners to co-operate in safeguarding and promoting the wellbeing of adults (and, for children, under separate provisions).
A statutory advocate who represents and supports a person who lacks capacity to make certain serious decisions and has no-one else appropriate to consult.
The Department for Education's statutory safeguarding guidance that schools and colleges in England must have regard to.
The former statutory body coordinating local safeguarding of children; replaced from 2019 by multi-agency safeguarding arrangements led by three safeguarding partners.
The statutory arrangements through which police, probation and prison services jointly assess and manage the risks posed by violent and sexual offenders.
The Act that provides the legal framework for making decisions on behalf of adults who lack the capacity to make particular decisions for themselves.
The Act governing the assessment, treatment and rights of people with a mental disorder, including detention ('sectioning') in hospital.

entries.term: Mental Health Act Code of Practice
entries.full_term: Mental Health Act Code of Practice
aliases: Mental Health Act Code of Practice
entries.definition: The statutory guidance on how the Mental Health Act 1983 should be applied, which professionals must have regard to.
entries.source: Department of Health (2015), under Mental Health Act 1983, s.118

entries.full_term: Detention under the Mental Health Act 1983
aliases: detained under the Mental Health Act
entries.definition: Everyday term for being detained in hospital for assessment or treatment under a section of the Mental Health Act 1983 without the person's consent; the number (for example 'sectioned under s.2') refers to the section of the Act being used.

entries.full_term: Section 2 Mental Health Act 1983 — admission for assessment
entries.definition: Detention for assessment (and any treatment that follows) for up to 28 days, on the recommendation of two doctors and an Approved Mental Health Professional; it cannot be renewed.

entries.full_term: Section 3 Mental Health Act 1983 — admission for treatment
entries.definition: Detention for treatment of a mental disorder, lasting up to six months initially and renewable, on the recommendation of two doctors and an Approved Mental Health Professional; it entitles the person to free s.117 aftercare on discharge.

entries.full_term: Section 136 Mental Health Act 1983 — police power to a place of safety
entries.definition: The police power to remove a person who appears to have a mental disorder and to be in immediate need of care or control from a public place to a place of safety so they can be assessed; time-limited to 24 hours (extendable to 36).

The joint duty on the NHS and the local authority to provide free aftercare to a person who has been detained for treatment (for example under s.3), for as long as they need it, to reduce the risk of readmission; amended by the Mental Health Act 2025, not yet in force.

entries.full_term: Section 17 Mental Health Act 1983 — leave of absence
entries.definition: Authorised leave of absence from hospital for a detained patient, granted by the responsible clinician; it may be for a few hours or longer and can carry conditions.

A social worker or other approved professional (not a doctor) who coordinates a Mental Health Act assessment, decides whether detention is the least restrictive option and makes most applications for detention.

The approved clinician with overall responsibility for a detained patient's case. An Approved Clinician is a professional (often but not always a psychiatrist) approved to take on certain Mental Health Act roles; the Responsible Clinician is the Approved Clinician in charge of a particular patient.
entries.source: Mental Health Act 1983, s.34 (and the MHA Code of Practice)

entries.definition: An order that lets a patient who has been detained for treatment live in the community under conditions, with the power to recall them to hospital if needed; also called supervised community treatment.

A specific relative, identified by a statutory list in the Mental Health Act, who has certain rights when a person is detained — including being consulted and, in some cases, objecting to detention or applying for discharge. It is distinct from next of kin.

entries.full_term: Guardianship under the Mental Health Act 1983
entries.definition: An order appointing a guardian (usually the local authority) with limited powers over where a person lives and their access to services, used to help someone with a mental disorder live safely in the community.

The independent judicial body that reviews whether a person's detention or community treatment under the Mental Health Act is still justified and can order their discharge; in England it is the First-tier Tribunal (Mental Health).
A place — usually a hospital, and only exceptionally a police station — to which someone can be taken for a Mental Health Act assessment under s.135 or s.136.
The Mental Health Act's broad legal definition — any disorder or disability of the mind — which determines who the Act can apply to; dependence on alcohol or drugs alone does not count.

A person receiving mental-health treatment in hospital who has agreed to be there and is not detained under the Act, and so is generally free to leave; contrasted with a detained (formal or sectioned) patient.

A doctor approved as having special experience in the diagnosis or treatment of mental disorder, whose recommendation is required for detention under the Mental Health Act; at least one of the two doctors in an assessment must be s.12 approved.

Whether a person is able to make a particular decision at the time it needs to be made. A person lacks capacity if an impairment of, or disturbance in, the mind or brain means they cannot understand, retain, use or weigh the relevant information, or communicate their decision. Capacity is assessed decision by decision and is assumed unless shown otherwise.

The principle that any decision or action taken for a person who lacks capacity must be in their best interests, weighing their past and present wishes, feelings, beliefs and values and following a statutory checklist.

The legal process for authorising arrangements that deprive a person who lacks capacity of their liberty in a care home or hospital, to make sure the arrangements are necessary and in their best interests. Due to be replaced by the Liberty Protection Safeguards (LPS) under the Mental Capacity (Amendment) Act 2019, not yet in force.

A legal document by which a person, while they still have capacity, appoints one or more attorneys to make decisions on their behalf if they later lose capacity — either for property and financial affairs, or for health and welfare.
The specialist court that makes decisions, and appoints deputies, for people who lack the capacity to make particular decisions about their finances or their welfare.
A person appointed by the Court of Protection to make ongoing decisions on behalf of someone who lacks capacity, where no attorney has been appointed under a Lasting Power of Attorney.

A decision made by a person while they have capacity to refuse a specified medical treatment in future, which is legally binding if valid and applicable. It differs from an advance statement, which records wishes and preferences but is not legally binding.

entries.term: Mental Capacity Act Code of Practice
entries.full_term: Mental Capacity Act Code of Practice
aliases: Mental Capacity Act Code of Practice
entries.definition: The statutory guidance on how the Mental Capacity Act should be applied, which professionals and paid carers must have regard to.
A statutory advocate who helps a person detained under the Mental Health Act (or on a community treatment order or guardianship) understand their rights and be heard in decisions about their care.

A person appointed to represent and support someone subject to a Deprivation of Liberty Safeguards authorisation, keeping in contact with them and helping them use their rights to review and challenge it.

Someone independent who supports a person to express their views, understand their options and defend their rights, especially when the person might otherwise struggle to be heard. Some advocacy roles are statutory (such as IMHA, IMCA and Care Act advocates); others are non-statutory.
A person-centred, outcomes-focused approach to adult safeguarding that works with the person to achieve the outcomes they want. Distinct from My Sister's Place (also 'MSP').
entries.source: Local Government Association / ADASS — Making Safeguarding Personal; reflected in Care Act 2014 statutory guidance.

entries.definition: A multi-agency group that shares intelligence and coordinates action on the quality and safety of local health and care services.
entries.source: NHS England — Quality Surveillance Group guidance.

entries.definition: The statutory multi-agency board that oversees and coordinates adult safeguarding arrangements in a local area.
entries.context_note: Locally, the Teeswide Safeguarding Adults Board.

entries.definition: A statutory review a Safeguarding Adults Board must arrange when an adult with care and support needs dies or is seriously harmed and abuse or neglect is suspected, to identify learning.
The recognised body responsible for governing and regulating a particular sport nationally.
The bodies that set standards for, accredit or regulate a profession or field of practice.
A group-based, participative approach to treatment in which the community itself is the primary therapeutic agent, used in mental-health, substance-use and offender settings.
entries.source: Royal College of Psychiatrists — Community of Communities.

entries.definition: A notice requiring a person or body to stop or take action about behaviour that is unreasonable and has a detrimental effect on the local community's quality of life. Distinct from Community Psychiatric Nurse (also 'CPN').
entries.source: Anti-social Behaviour, Crime and Policing Act 2014, s.43

entries.definition: An NHS commissioning support unit providing business intelligence, analytics and data services to NHS and public-health bodies across the North East and beyond.

The UK's national statistical institute and largest producer of official statistics — population, the census, the economy and the labour market — operating at arm's length under the UK Statistics Authority.
The Office for National Statistics decennial census of England and Wales, taken on 21 March 2021; the definitive small-area source for population, households and demographics.
The UK government department responsible for transport policy; publishes national transport, road-traffic and road-safety statistics.
The national system, run by the Office for Health Improvement and Disparities (OHID), that collects data on people in drug and alcohol treatment in England.
entries.source: OHID — National Drug Treatment Monitoring System (NDTMS)

entries.definition: A continuous Office for National Statistics household survey providing labour-market, employment and related estimates for local areas.
The national framework of measures of adult social care outcomes in England, published annually by NHS England (formerly NHS Digital).
entries.source: NHS England — Adult Social Care Outcomes Framework (ASCOF)

entries.definition: Great Britain's national mapping agency (a government-owned company).

entries.term: UK local and regional greenhouse gas emissions statistics
entries.full_term: UK local authority and regional greenhouse gas emissions statistics
aliases: UK local authority and regional greenhouse gas emissions statistics
entries.definition: National Statistics published by the Department for Energy Security and Net Zero (DESNZ) giving estimated territorial greenhouse gas emissions for each local authority area.
entries.source: DESNZ (GOV.UK) — UK local authority and regional greenhouse gas emissions statistics

entries.term: ONS Crime data (Community Safety Partnership area)
entries.full_term: Crime data by Community Safety Partnership area (ONS)
aliases: Crime data by Community Safety Partnership area
entries.definition: Office for National Statistics recorded-crime statistics published at Community Safety Partnership / local-authority level.
entries.source: ONS — Crime in England and Wales

entries.definition: The national arm's-length body that invests public and National Lottery funding in grassroots sport and physical activity in England.
A national survey of physical-activity levels among adults and children in England.
The government's statutory adviser for the natural environment in England.
The independent regulator for Britain's railways and monitor of National Highways; publishes rail-usage and station-usage statistics.

entries.full_term: Youth Justice Board for England and Wales
aliases: Youth Justice Board for England and Wales
entries.definition: The arm's-length body that oversees the youth justice system in England and Wales and publishes youth justice statistics.
entries.source: GOV.UK — Youth Justice Board for England and Wales

entries.definition: The British Association for Parenteral and Enteral Nutrition (BAPEN)'s five-step screening tool to identify adults who are malnourished or at risk of malnutrition and agree a care plan.
The Office for National Statistics rapid omnibus survey of adults in Great Britain, covering opinions, behaviours and wellbeing (e.g. internet access, loneliness).
An arm's-length body sponsored by the Department for Work and Pensions providing free money and pensions guidance (MoneyHelper).
The Money and Pensions Service national survey of adults' financial wellbeing across the United Kingdom, covering saving, borrowing and financial resilience.
entries.source: Money and Pensions Service — Adult Financial Wellbeing Survey

entries.definition: Official statistics on the number and proportion of households in fuel poverty in England, available by local area, published by the Department for Energy Security and Net Zero (DESNZ).
The national team (operating as Stop Loan Sharks) that investigates illegal money lending and supports victims of loan sharks in England.
entries.source: Stop Loan Sharks — the England Illegal Money Lending Team

entries.definition: An independent statistics website that repackages Office for National Statistics and other public data into local-area profiles and charts.
The executive non-departmental public body responsible for flood risk, water quality and environmental protection in England.

entries.term: Department for Environment, Food & Rural Affairs
entries.full_term: Department for Environment, Food & Rural Affairs
aliases: Department for Environment, Food & Rural Affairs
Department for Environment Food & Rural Affairs
entries.definition: The UK government department responsible for environmental protection, food and farming, and rural affairs.
entries.source: GOV.UK — Department for Environment, Food & Rural Affairs

entries.definition: The single UK government website through which departments publish services, guidance and official statistics.
The national GP pay-for-performance framework whose data provides recorded prevalence of long-term conditions; published by NHS England (formerly NHS Digital).
entries.source: NHS England — Quality and Outcomes Framework (QOF)

entries.definition: A near-real-time / syndromic-surveillance data system operated by North of England Commissioning Support (NECS), used to monitor health indicators and pressures locally.
Office for National Statistics annual statistics on conceptions (including under-18 conceptions) for England and Wales, available by local area.
entries.source: ONS — Conception statistics, England and Wales

entries.definition: A not-for-profit organisation, formerly Happy City, that develops place-based wellbeing measures and supports local areas to improve wellbeing.
A place-based wellbeing measure that scores local areas on the conditions for wellbeing, sustainability and equality.
entries.source: Centre for Thriving Places — Thriving Places Index

entries.definition: The professional body for policing in England and Wales, setting standards, guidance and training for the police service.
An evidence resource that summarises what works to reduce crime, rating interventions by the strength and direction of the underlying evidence.
entries.source: College of Policing — Crime Reduction Toolkit

entries.definition: The former public-spending watchdog for local government and the NHS in England, abolished on 31 March 2015.
The Office for National Statistics and Department for Work and Pensions monthly count of people claiming unemployment-related benefits.

entries.full_term: Cleveland Unit for the Reduction of Violence
aliases: Cleveland Unit for the Reduction of Violence
entries.definition: Cleveland's Violence Reduction Unit, hosted by the Office of the Police and Crime Commissioner, taking a public-health, multi-agency approach to reducing serious violence.
entries.source: Cleveland Police and Crime Commissioner — CURV

entries.term: Cleveland Serious Violence Strategic Needs Assessment
entries.full_term: Cleveland Serious Violence Strategic Needs Assessment
aliases: Cleveland Serious Violence Strategic Needs Assessment
entries.definition: The assessment of serious violence across the Cleveland area, produced to inform the local serious-violence strategy under the Serious Violence Duty.
entries.source: CURV — Cleveland Serious Violence Strategic Needs Assessment

entries.definition: A national network of independent local charities offering free, confidential and impartial advice on money, benefits, housing, employment and legal matters; known historically as the Citizens Advice Bureau (CAB).
The local Citizens Advice office providing free, independent advice (debt, benefits, housing) in Middlesbrough.

entries.term: Citizens Advice Darlington, Redcar and Cleveland
entries.full_term: Citizens Advice Darlington, Redcar and Cleveland
aliases: Citizens Advice Darlington, Redcar and Cleveland
entries.definition: The local Citizens Advice office providing free, independent advice across Darlington, Redcar and Cleveland.
entries.source: Citizens Advice Darlington, Redcar and Cleveland

entries.definition: A physical-education teaching-resources provider.
An Institute of Public Care tool that projects the population of older people and related needs for local areas.

entries.term: NE Regional Road Safety Resource / TADU
entries.full_term: North East Regional Road Safety Resource / Traffic and Accident Data Unit
aliases: North East Regional Road Safety Resource
entries.definition: The North East regional road-safety data resource and Traffic and Accident Data Unit, providing road-collision and casualty data for the region.
entries.source: North East Regional Road Safety Resource / TADU

entries.definition: The United Nations specialised agency for international public health.
The Local Government Association's free (LG Inform) and subscription (LG Inform Plus) data-benchmarking service, presenting local-authority performance and area data.

entries.full_term: Youth Offending Service Case Management System
entries.definition: The local Youth Offending Service's case-management record of young people in the youth justice system.
entries.source: Local Youth Offending Service (Middlesbrough / Redcar & Cleveland)

entries.definition: The United States non-profit for Alzheimer's care, support and research.
The national membership body for councils in England and Wales; publishes local-area data (LG Inform) and sector policy.
A local evidence study of housing need and demand across a housing-market area, used to inform housing and planning policy and Local Plans.
The professional association and registered trade union for doctors in the UK.
A specialist health and social care research, consultancy and analysis unit based at Oxford Brookes University.
entries.source: Institute of Public Care, Oxford Brookes University

entries.full_term: British Association for Parenteral and Enteral Nutrition
aliases: British Association for Parenteral and Enteral Nutrition
entries.definition: A multi-professional association and registered charity concerned with the recognition, prevention and treatment of malnutrition and with nutritional care.
entries.source: British Association for Parenteral and Enteral Nutrition (BAPEN)

entries.definition: On the internationally standard International Labour Organization (ILO) measure — the survey measure the Office for National Statistics produces from the Labour Force Survey and Annual Population Survey — people aged 16 and over who are out of work, have actively sought work in the past four weeks, and are available to start within two weeks. It is a survey estimate, distinct from the benefits-based [[ONS Claimant Count]].
entries.source: ONS — A guide to labour market statistics
entries.context_note: A survey estimate with wide margins for small areas that cannot identify individual non-claiming jobseekers, so local employment and skills delivery does not use it — work is driven by the [[ONS Claimant Count]] and by economic-inactivity rates.

entries.definition: In Office for National Statistics labour-market statistics, people aged 16 to 64 who are neither in employment nor unemployed — out of work and either not seeking work or not available to start — for example students, people looking after family or home, the long-term sick, and the retired.
entries.source: ONS — A guide to labour market statistics
entries.context_note: The measure local employment and skills work targets in practice — the [[Local Skills Improvement Plan]] is charged with reducing it. Because a non-claiming jobseeker cannot be identified locally, out-of-work people absent from the [[ONS Claimant Count]] are in practice treated here rather than as unemployed, even though the survey-based [[Unemployment]] measure would formally class an active, available jobseeker as unemployed regardless of claiming.

entries.definition: A statutory, employer-led plan setting out the current and future skills and workforce needs of a local area to shape post-16 technical education and training, placed on a statutory footing by the Skills and Post-16 Education Act 2022.
entries.source: Skills and Post-16 Education Act 2022 (Part 1, Chapter 1)

entries.term: North East England Chamber of Commerce
entries.full_term: North East England Chamber of Commerce
aliases: North East England Chamber of Commerce
entries.definition: The accredited chamber of commerce representing businesses across North East England.
entries.source: North East England Chamber of Commerce
